newsitem.title: UK: Brazil to play key role in new MATIF sugar contracT.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to play key role in new MATIF sugar contracT.

text.p: Brazil and central America will be pivotal for the success of the new lesser-quality white sugar futures contract to be launched in Paris later this month, French officials said on Thursday.

Bruno Guiot, Commodities Product Manager at the Marche a Terme International de France (MATIF), said demand was evident for a 100 ICUMSA contract from the trade and producers to reflect world sugar flows.
"The world sugar market experienced a large move over 10 years and in the futures market nothing was done to reflect this," Guiot told a London news conference.
"The demand for this contract appeared two years ago when Brazil started to export these sugars in a massive way. Brazil and central America will play a key role."
Brazil, Thailand and Guatemala had all roughly doubled their white sugar production since 1989/90. Brazil's white sugar exports had surged more than eight-fold in the period, Guiot said.
But the impact the new contract would have on south Asian sugar markets is unclear as yet as there was no freight differential to apply.
MATIF had launched a feasibility study to investigate a new contract to reflect world market changes.
These included the elimination of state-controlled marketing structures in key producing nations such as Brazil and the privatisation of purchase infrastructures in main importing countries, he said.
Guiot estimated the total amount of white sugar which could theoretically be hedged against the new pit-based contract at five million tonnes a year.
But he said the exchange did not expect hedge funds or financial investors to be active in the contract in the early days as liquidity would be low and return on investment was likely to be limited.
Trading in the new MATIF sugar contract is scheduled to start on the October 1997 expiry on June 20.
Sugars with ratings close to 100 ICUMSA are mainly produced in South America, Central America and Asia and currently account for over a third of world sugar trade.
Other sugars with ICUMSA ratings of under 45 are mainly produced in Europe.
ICUMSA (International Commission for Uniform Method of Sugar Analysis) ratings measure the colouring of sugar and are an indication of quality.

MATIF, founded in February 1986, is one of the world's largest financial futures and options exchanges with more than 68 million contracts traded in 1996, including more than 272,000 commodities contracts.
